statement: For all functions f,D: ℝ → ℝ and all x,h,L ∈ ℝ with h > 0 and L ≥ 0, if f is continuous on [x,x+h], has derivative D(t) at each t in (x,x+h), and satisfies |D(t)−D(x)| ≤ L|t−x| for every such t, then the constructed quotient (f(x+h)−f(x))/h satisfies |(f(x+h)−f(x))/h−D(x)| ≤ Lh. No hypothesis asserts that D(x) is a derivative of f at x.

targets.name: Research.forwardDifference_error_bound
targets.statement: For every f: ℝ → ℝ, every D: ℝ → ℝ, and every x,h,L ∈ ℝ, assume (1) 0 < h; (2) 0 ≤ L; (3) f is continuous on [x,x+h] = {t ∈ ℝ : x ≤ t ≤ x+h} in the usual real topology; (4) for every t ∈ ℝ with x < t < x+h, f has ordinary two-sided derivative D(t) at t; and (5) for every t ∈ ℝ with x < t < x+h, |D(t)−D(x)| ≤ L|t−x|. Then |Research.forwardDifference(f,x,h)−D(x)| ≤ Lh. Substituting the supplied definition, this is |(f(x+h)−f(x))/h−D(x)| ≤ Lh. The value D(x) is the value of the arbitrary supplied function D at x. Derivatives at the endpoints, continuity of D, and a pairwise Lipschitz inequality for D are not additional hypotheses.

constructions.name: Research.forwardDifference
constructions.description: This function has domain (ℝ → ℝ) × ℝ × ℝ and codomain ℝ (expressed as a curried function). For any f: ℝ → ℝ and x,h ∈ ℝ it returns (f(x+h)−f(x))/h: it evaluates f at x+h and x, subtracts f(x), then divides by h. The definition has no hypotheses on f, x, or h. For nonzero h this is the secant slope between x and x+h; it takes no limit. Under Lean real division, which is total with inverse of zero equal to zero, the value at h=0 is zero. The target theorem applies this exact construction under the additional restriction h > 0.

assumptions: All functions f,D: ℝ → ℝ and all real parameters x,h,L are universally quantified in the theorem.
The theorem assumes 0 < h and 0 ≤ L.
The theorem assumes f is continuous on the closed interval [x,x+h].
For every real t in the open interval (x,x+h), the theorem assumes that f has derivative D(t) at t.
For every real t in the open interval (x,x+h), the theorem assumes |D(t)−D(x)| ≤ L|t−x|.
The construction imposes no hypotheses and uses ordinary real arithmetic with Lean’s total convention for division by zero.
